making employment arbitration mandatory has an adverse effect on applicants' attraction, and this adverse effect can be mitigated when the arbitration procedures are more just and when employees are provided with just-cause protection.
mandatory employment arbitration has negative effects on applicant attraction, and these effects can be moderated by the procedural and substantive characteristics of arbitration systems.

(1) making employment arbitration mandatory was negatively related to organizational attraction, (2) this relationship was mitigated when due process considerations were afforded to employees, (3) this relationship was further mitigated when just-cause protections were given to employees, and (4) this relationship was more negative for minorities than nonminority applicants.
